title: Harbor and Tide
premise: Noor Amberdale, a ghostwriter drowning in debt and self-erasure, is hired to write the memoirs of orchard magnate Elias Vane — only to discover his estranged daughter, Marisol, holds half the deed to the very orchard where Noor's failing bakery lease depends. As Noor shuttles between father and daughter, mining their wounds for material while quietly falling for Marisol, she realizes she's been weaponizing other people's stories to avoid writing her own. When Elias's memoir threatens to bury Marisol's version of the truth, Noor must choose between her contract and her conscience, exposing her own betrayal in the process. In the end, she forfeits the ghostwriting fee, co-signs a new lease with Marisol on honest terms, and publishes her first novel under her own name.
about_author: Beatrix Sandoval spent a decade as an uncredited ghostwriter for celebrity memoirs before turning her pen toward fiction about people who live in the margins of other people's stories. She writes from a converted fruit-packing shed on the coast, where the tide keeps better time than she does.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She delivers a finished memoir to a client who takes full credit at a launch party, then returns to her struggling bakery above the harbor to find an eviction notice tucked in the mail slot. The beat: quiet humiliation sharpening into desperation.

chapters.title: An Offer Written in Someone Else's Ink
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Literary agent Dev offers her the Vane memoir — double her usual rate, enough to save the bakery lease. The catch: Elias Vane is notoriously impossible, and the deadline coincides exactly with her lease renewal. Beat: hope arriving dressed as a trap.

chapters.title: The Orchard That Refuses to Die
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. At the neglected Vane orchard, Elias walks rows of blighted trees he cannot bring himself to cut down, dictating bitter memories into a recorder. He mentions a deed clause involving his estranged daughter. Beat: grief calcified into stubbornness.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Stubborn Deed
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol arrives from the city intending to sell her inherited half of the orchard fast, only to learn the deed binds both halves to shared decisions for one year. She meets Noor snooping through the estate office. Beat: instant friction, grudging curiosity.

chapters.title: Interviews and Interrogations
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor begins formal sessions with Elias, but his answers are performance; meanwhile Marisol keeps appearing, poking holes in her father's polished anecdotes. Noor starts keeping two sets of notes. Beat: the thrill of access curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A storm floods the orchard's lower field, unearthing an old boat and a box of Marisol's mother's letters that Elias never destroyed. Marisol reads them overnight. Beat: the past surfacing literally, demanding witness.

chapters.title: Bread and Bad Faith
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Marisol shows up at Noor's bakery at closing time; over leftover sourdough they argue about whether Elias deserves redemption. It ends in laughter neither expected. Beat: first warmth, immediately distrusted by both.

chapters.title: The Chapter That Isn't True
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias dictates a chapter blaming his late wife for the family rupture; Noor, knowing the letters say otherwise, types it anyway. Alone afterward she rereads her own abandoned novel draft and deletes nothing, which feels worse. Beat: moral erosion made concrete.

chapters.title: Lease Terms, Heart Terms
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol offers to buy out Noor's bakery building if Noor helps her contest the deed — using what she learns from Elias's sessions. Noor refuses, then can't stop thinking about it. Beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Ghostwriter, Haunt Thyself
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Dev pressures Noor for scandalous material to boost pre-sales; she realizes every career move she's ever made has been someone else's story told louder. She visits her mother, seeking absolution, and gets honesty instead. Beat: confrontation with the person in the mirror.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias and Marisol are forced by the deed to jointly decide which trees to fell; working side by side, old tenderness flickers until he says something unforgivable about her mother. Beat: reconciliation glimpsed, then burned.

chapters.title: The Draft Leaks
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A partial manuscript — including the false chapter — reaches a journalist. Marisol assumes Noor leaked it deliberately; Elias assumes Marisol stole it. Noor knows the leak came from Dev's office. Beat: betrayal triangulated, trust shattered.

chapters.title: Silence Is Also a Contract
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Dev offers Noor a promotion and legal protection if she stays quiet about the leak's source. The bakery landlord extends her lease — suspiciously — courtesy of Dev. Beat: the price of survival itemized, and it's her integrity.

chapters.title: Reading the Letters Aloud
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol confronts Elias with her mother's letters at the orchard gate; for the first time he listens without interrupting, and breaks. He admits the memoir was his attempt to control the record before dying. Beat: truth disarming power.

chapters.title: The Confession Nobody Hired Her For
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor tells Marisol everything: the false chapter, the two sets of notes, the deal she almost took. She expects exile and instead receives a condition — help us tell it right, publicly. Beat: forgiveness offered only after honesty, not instead of it.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The trio plots to preempt the memoir's release: Elias will publish a retraction chapter, Marisol will go public with the letters, and Noor will testify to Dev's manipulation — burning her career bridges. Beat: three damaged people choosing consequence over safety.

chapters.title: Dev Comes Collecting
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Dev threatens litigation and blacklisting, revealing he engineered the bakery's financial ruin to leash her all along. Noor records the conversation. Beat: the villain unmasked as the system itself, and Noor finally stops flinching.

chapters.title: The Reading at the Cider House
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At the orchard's old cider house, Elias reads the true final chapter aloud to townsfolk and press while Marisol displays the letters; Noor stands beside them, named openly as collaborator, not ghost. Beat: public reckoning as communal healing.

chapters.title: Ash and Graft
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The blighted trees come down; Elias teaches Marisol to graft healthy stock onto old root systems — his clumsy metaphor for inheritance and repair. He signs papers transferring decision-making power to her. Beat: power relinquished before death can take it.

chapters.title: What Noor Wrote
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. With the lease lost and savings gone, Noor finishes her own novel in six weeks at the bakery's empty counter, writing her mother's story and her own in the same breath. Dev's lawsuit collapses on her recording. Beat: the mirror finally forgivable.

chapters.title: Harbor and Tide
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Spring: the grafted trees blossom. Marisol and Noor sign a joint lease — bakery below, writing room above — on terms read aloud to each other like vows. First kiss among the blossoms, unhurried. Beat: love built on disclosed flaws, not despite them.

chapters.title: Under My Own Name
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue. At her first book event, someone asks Noor who she really is; she answers plainly, and Elias and Marisol sit in the third row. The tide comes in on schedule outside. Beat: arrival — second chances, it turns out, were always about timing she chose herself.
